description.narrative: Since January 20, 2025, security in eastern DRC has deteriorated due to M23 offensives in North and South Kivu, displacing over 400,000 people, 41% of whom are school-aged children.The fall of Goma on January 27th exacerbated the crisis, leaving displaced populations in extreme vulnerability sheltering in host families, abandoned buildings, churches, and schools with minimal access to water, food, healthcare, and shelter. Women and children face heightened risks of GBV, exploitation, and community violence, while humanitarian infrastructure is overwhelmed. Help a Child (HaC) will target Goma and Nyiragongo health zones in North Kivu to address urgent humanitarian needs. A February 1, 2025, assessment revealed a near-total collapse of basic services. Electricity and potable water are cut off, forcing reliance on untreated water and increasing cholera risks. Morgues are full, bodies remain on street, and looted humanitarian warehouses hinder emergency efforts. While 60% of displaced people are returning, many remain stranded due to insecurity, financial constraints, and lack of shelter. Priority needs that Help a Child and local partners ADED and Collectif Alpha Juvi (CAU) will address persist in food security, requiring access to food through MPC to prevent malnutrition. WASH, preventing diseases and improving sanitation with emergency latrines, hygiene awareness campaigns, and WASH/Hygiene kits including menstrual health items. Besides that, Protection concerns are critical, particularly for women and children vulnerable to gender-based violence (GBV) and human trafficking, necessitating safe spaces, psychological support, and family reunification mechanisms for unaccompanied children. Beyond immediate relief, we aim to enhance crisis response capacities and implement return and reintegration strategies, ensuring safe, dignified returns and restoring essential services in host communities.

title.narrative: Number of people benefitting from unconditional and unrestricted cash transfers

description.narrative: Unconditional transfers are provided to beneficiaries without the recipient having to do anything in return in order to receive the assistance . Unrestricted transfers can be used entirely as the recipient chooses i.e. there are no restrictions on how the transfer is spent (Definitions of CALP). It can be delivered e.g. through local banks, shops, traders, local money transfer companies, remittance companies and post offices in either one or several instalments. Please include in the activity description the amount and frequency of cash transfers (i.e. how often). In case beneficiaries receive multiple transfers (e.g. each month), please only count the beneficiaries once.

title.narrative: Number of unaccompanied and/or separated children who are reunited with their caregivers OR in appropriate protective care arrangements based on BIA

description.narrative: 1) Care arrangements can include temporary care arrangements in host family or other care arrangements.2) Appropriate means (but is not limited to) that care arrangements must take into account different needs of children based on their age, sex and diversity. Morevoer they must as much as possible be defined taking into account the specificities of the context and - when appropriate - be built on existing coping mechanisms. 3) Appropriate is related to the physical safety and psychosocial well-being of the child. Specific attention should be put on non-discrimination of fostered children compared to biological ones. 4) Unaccompanied and/or separated children must be disaggegated by age and sex. This indicator excludes the reunification of other family members (above 18) which is to be reported under PRO-R14

title.narrative: Number of children that received support specified to their needs

description.narrative: 1) This indicator covers response to children (girls and boys under 18). 2) Appropriate response is defined as the provision of comprehensive services/assistance based on a thorough analysis of the risks faced by persons. The protection outcome of the response must be well defined. Relevant SOPs (including functional Referral Mechanism) should be followed. 3) Use the activity description field to to describe what services (medical, MHPSS, legal, security, etc.), as well as SOPs are in place. Activities can include psychosocial support to children, Child Friendly Spaces and support to parents to fulfill their protection responsibilities towards their children. 4) Number of persons must be disaggregated by sex at reporting stage.5) If action also includes prevention activities, please describe this within the activity under this indicator.If relevant, please specify in the activity description your target population, for example child soldiers.

title.narrative: Number of people having access to sufficient and safe water for domestic use

description.narrative: Access: maximum distance to water point 500m, queuing time less than 15min, filling time maximum 3 min/20 litres or as locally agreed. Water access should be during the whole period of implementation unless action is mostly related to building the local water delivery capacity. Sufficient: covering basic needs, i.e. 7.5-15 l/p/d or as locally agreed. Safe: 1) low risk of faecal contamination, 2) No faecal coliforms detectable in any 100-ml sample, 3) For piped water supplies, or for all water supplies at times of risk or presence of diarrhoea epidemic, water is treated with a disinfectant to achieve free chlorine residual at the tap of 0.5 mg per litre and turbidity is below 5 NTU, 4) If for a short period, water which is contaminated chemically or radiologically is used, no (significant probability of) negative health effect is (likely to be) detected. Domestic use: drinking, cooking and personal hygiene (incl. laundry)

title.narrative: Number of people having access to dignified, safe, clean and functional excreta disposal facilities

description.narrative: Access: ratio (user/facility) of 1 toilet for a max. 20 people, distance < 50 metres from dwellings, or as locally agreed. Clean: regular cleaning and maintenance for public facilities.Dignified: Use of toilets respect cultural preference and is arranged by household(s) and/or segregated by sex. Unsafe facilities: unstable (unlined) pits with risk of collapse, pits accessible to vectors, pits contaminating water tables and poorly sited facilities which expose women and girls to attacks, especially at night. Functional facility: fully constructed, in working order and properly maintained, of a type and in a location acceptable to intended users, with hand washing facilities and anal cleansing material.

title.narrative: Number of people having regular access to soap to meet hygienic needs

description.narrative: Regular and timely access: 250g soap/p/m for personal hygiene, 200g soap/p/month for laundry. This includes hygiene/dignity kits. Access may be in-kind or though voucher distribution or through unconditional restricted cash to enable beneficiary to buy soap (without compromising access to other basic needs). Distributed items need to be culturally acceptable i.e. take into account local practice and expectations.
